mode: preseason dry-run (no games played yet; Week 1 opens Sept. 9-14) — stash candidates from the full unrostered pool, priced as if pursued now, not weekly pickups
note: All ten rosters still show $0 FAAB used and no waiver transactions this season — every price below is a speculative pre-Week-1 stash bid, not a contested-market read. Recheck once real snap counts exist.

targets.why: Named the Saints' presumptive WR3 behind Chris Olave and rookie Jordyn Tyson; coach Kellen Moore has said publicly he regrets not featuring Vele more in 2025 and plans to lean on him more in Year 2 (Yahoo Sports, Aug. 2026). He closed 2025 hot — 18 of 25 targets over a four-game stretch — before a December IR stint.
targets.asset: WR3 in a Kellen Moore offense with real target share upside if Olave misses time; no live 2026 games yet to confirm the role holds against rookie competition (Tyson, Bryce Lance).
targets.my_team_impact: Doesn't crack my Week 1 lineup — Pickens/Egbuka/Odunze/Boutte/Johnston already fill 5 WR-eligible bench-or-starter spots. Would only be added as a pure speculative stash over my weakest WR bench piece (Johnston or Boutte).
targets.confidence_why: Named role plus a real late-2025 target trend, but zero 2026 regular-season snaps yet to confirm it survives the rookie competition.
targets.competition: No other roster carries a Saints skill-position piece besides DiaperDutyDaddy's Travis Etienne (RB) — no direct WR3 competitor in-league.
targets.bid: 3 dollars — routine-uncontested band, no rival pressure spotted
targets.drop: None recommended for me; league-wide, a WR-thin roster's WR5/6 is the natural drop.

targets.why: Confirmed as Baltimore's clear RB2/passing-down back behind Derrick Henry for 2026 (CBS Sports, RotoWire); has stayed healthy through camp and preseason while rookie Adam Randall battles him for early-down change-of-pace work, not the passing-down role itself.
targets.asset: Henry's direct backup and the pass-catching-back piece in Baltimore's offense — realistic 8-12 touch/target FLEX-dart weeks if Henry (37 in November) needs a breather or misses time.
targets.my_team_impact: Doesn't crack my lineup — I don't roster Henry or any Ravens piece, so this is pure handcuff-for-someone-else value rather than a fit for my RB corps (Taylor/Jeanty/Irving/Tuten/Washington already covers 5 RB slots).
targets.confidence_why: Real role but zero standalone value unless Henry is out — a correct handcuff for mfkr (who rosters Henry), not a fit for my roster.
targets.competition: mfkr owns Derrick Henry and is the one rival who should actually want this FAAB spend as direct handcuff insurance.
targets.bid: n/a for me — flagging for mfkr's benefit, not a bid I'd place
targets.drop: N/A — not a fit for my roster.

targets.why: The 33-year-old unretired-then-traded veteran signed with Carolina this offseason to work with new offensive specialist Darrell Bevell; per ESPN/NFL.com he projects as at least a red-zone specialist in a room fronted by Tommy Tremble, with real name value from a 6-TD, 9-game stretch in Miami last year.
targets.asset: Streaky red-zone TE1/2 upside if he wins real snaps over Tremble; unproven target-share floor behind a new starter in a crowded room, and this format's shallow TE market (no bench TE at 7 of 10 rosters) makes any real role notable.
targets.my_team_impact: Doesn't crack my lineup — LaPorta and Ferguson already give me a locked top-5 TE plus a real bench option. No fit here.
targets.confidence_why: Name value and a red-zone-role case, but no confirmed target share yet and he's clearly behind Tremble on early camp reporting.
targets.competition: Seven of ten rosters carry only one TE and would feel real pain from a bye or injury; none has moved yet since nobody's snap counts exist.
targets.bid: 2 dollars — routine-uncontested band for a name-value TE dart
targets.drop: League-wide: any single-TE roster's weakest bench piece.

targets.why: With Isiah Pacheco now on IR (this run's item), Detroit's RB depth behind Gibbs thins to Vaki and Jacob Saylors (the latter already rostered by Stipe and this week's single most-added player league-wide per Sleeper trending data). Reports still call Vaki primarily a special-teamer/kick returner with a 4.62 40 that limits his offensive translation.
targets.asset: Deep-bench dart on a top-3 offense's RB3 spot behind a true workhorse (Gibbs) — touches would only materialize on a Gibbs injury, and even then Saylors reads ahead of him on current camp buzz.
targets.my_team_impact: Doesn't crack my lineup — I don't roster any Lions RB, so this is speculative-only depth with no direct fit.
targets.confidence_why: No offensive role established, and Saylors (already gone off the wire) reads as the actual first man up if Gibbs is out.
targets.competition: Stipe already has the more-hyped handcuff (Saylors); little reason for a second roster to chase Vaki specifically.
targets.bid: 1 dollar if pursued at all — pure dart

targets.why: 6th-round rookie who's reportedly been the standout performer at Saints camp, flashing with the 1s and 2s as a pass-catcher on top of elite return ability (2nd in NCAA history in return TDs). Started camp projected as WR5/returner behind Vele but has out-performed that slotting so far.
targets.asset: Speculative dynasty-flavored dart with real special-teams floor (return value doesn't score in this format, but roster survival does) and a path to real snaps only if camp buzz keeps translating; no game washing yet.
targets.my_team_impact: Doesn't crack my lineup — same WR-depth math as Vele above; would be a pure late-bench dart over my weakest WR piece if I had space.
targets.confidence_why: Camp hype with zero regular-season or even preseason-game confirmation yet; behind Vele, Olave, and a first-round rookie (Tyson) on paper.
targets.competition: No rival has a stake in the Saints WR room beyond DiaperDutyDaddy's Etienne at RB.
